Neogotische kruisbasiliek van Pierre Cuy: Gothic Revival cruciform basilica by Pierre Cuypers, national monument
Kort nadat Ospel in 1864 een eigen paroc: Soon after Ospel became a parish of its own in 1864, Pierre Cuypers designed this brick cruciform basilica; it was consecrated in 1868. In 1944 the tower was blown up and the vaults destroyed. The new tower of 1954 has a slate spire between four corner turrets.

Een beltmolen uit 1870, op een plek waar: A mound mill from 1870, built where no mill had stood before. It ground grain until 1948, was stripped of its sails in 1970 and bought by the municipality in 1972. Since its restoration in 1990, volunteers grind grain here again, with two pairs of millstones.
Beltmolen uit 1840 in Kreijel, rijksmonu: Mound mill from 1840 in Kreijel, national monument
Twintig boeren lieten deze beltmolen in: Twenty farmers had this mound mill built in 1840. Around 1900 it got a suction gas engine, so it could grind when there was no wind. It worked as a corn mill until about 1970 and was restored in 1979. Its sails are 25 metres across.
Onze-Lieve-Vrouw-van-Altijddurende-Bijst: Chapel of Our Lady of Perpetual Help, national monument
In 1893 stond hier een coöperatief melkf: In 1893 a small cooperative dairy stood here, worked by hand, under the motto Unity is strength. When the steam dairy took over in 1906, the building was turned into a chapel, blessed in 1907. Inside, the wooden vault and the pews are painted blue.
De kapel in 2009, A. Ansems, publiek dom: The chapel in 2009, A. Ansems, public domain
In 1993 gingen de Heilig Hartschool en d: In 1993 the Heilig Hart school and the Sint-Anna school merged into De Schrank. The Heilig Hart school began in 1861 as a public primary school; the girls' school belonged to the Sint-Anna convent of the Franciscan sisters from Heythuysen, here from 1910 to 1959.
Bezoekerscentrum van Nationaal Park De G: Visitor centre of De Groote Peel National Park
De hoofdingang van Nationaal Park De Gro: The main entrance to De Groote Peel National Park, once called Mijl op Zeven: information, a terrace and the start of the walks into the raised bog. De Groote Peel has been a national park since 1993.
Hier stond de lagere school van Ospeldij: This was the primary school of Ospeldijk, first the Heilige Geest school, later 't Kienhout. It closed in 2012 for lack of pupils; now it is a Thomashuis, a small care home.
Pastoor Carels vierde in 1924 zijn zilve: Father Carels celebrated 25 years as Ospel's parish priest in 1924 and had this statue made by Albert Verschuuren. Christ blesses with his right hand; beside him kneel a woman with a child and a man with a sack on his shoulder. The little park it was placed in, in 1926, is now part of the churchyard.
Het Heilig Hartbeeld in 1935, publiek do: The Sacred Heart statue in 1935, public domain
Een driekante zuil van roestvrij staal b: A three-sided stainless steel column by the visitor centre, in memory of the aircrews who died in the Peel during the Second World War.
Een celtic field: de sporen van een preh: A celtic field: the traces of a prehistoric field system, small square fields with low banks around them, laid out between the late Bronze Age and Roman times.
Het sportpark van RKSVO, de voetbalclub: The grounds of RKSVO, Ospel's football club, founded in 1948.
Ospel ligt op hoge, zandige grond die al: Ospel lies on high, sandy ground that reached into the Peel marshes like a peninsula. The name comes from Espelo, aspen wood: aspens grew here. In 1840 Ospel was still a hamlet of 176 people.
In 1864 werd Ospel een eigen parochie, e: In 1864 Ospel became a parish of its own, and a village where the hamlets around it came for church, school and shop. Pierre Cuypers, the architect of the Rijksmuseum, designed the church: a brick Gothic Revival cruciform basilica, consecrated in 1868.
De kerk in 1971, H.P.R. Rosenberg, Rijks: The church in 1971, H.P.R. Rosenberg, Cultural Heritage Agency of the Netherlands, CC BY-SA 4.0
In 1944 werd de kerktoren opgeblazen en: In 1944 the church tower was blown up and the rib vaults collapsed. They were partly restored in 1946 and 1947; by 1954 a new tower stood, with a slate spire between four corner turrets and a hexagonal stair tower beside it. In 1956 a new Vermeulen organ followed.
De toren in 2001, J.P. de Koning, Rijksd: The tower in 2001, J.P. de Koning, Cultural Heritage Agency of the Netherlands, CC BY-SA 4.0
Het jonge dorp kreeg in 1870 een eigen k: In 1870 the young village got a corn mill of its own. De Korenbloem ground grain until 1948 and then fell into disrepair; in 1970 it lost its sails. The municipality bought it in 1972 and had it restored in 1990. Now volunteers grind grain here again.
De Korenbloem in verval, 1966, W.A. Korp: De Korenbloem in disrepair, 1966, W.A. Korpershoek, Cultural Heritage Agency of the Netherlands, CC BY-SA 4.0
In 1893 begonnen boeren aan de Klaarstra: In 1893 farmers on the Klaarstraat started a small cooperative dairy, worked by hand, under the motto Unity is strength. When the Sint-Isidorus steam dairy took over in 1906, the little building became a chapel to Our Lady of Perpetual Help, blessed in 1907.
Het blauwe interieur in 2012, A. Ansems,: The blue interior in 2012, A. Ansems, CC BY-SA 3.0 NL
Twintig boeren uit de buurt lieten in Kr: Twenty local farmers had a mound mill built in Kreijel to grind their own grain. Around 1900 it got a suction gas engine, so it could run when there was no wind. It ground until about 1970 and was restored in 1979, with sails 25 metres across.
Vanaf 1803 liet Napoleon een kanaal grav: From 1803 Napoleon had a canal dug from the Scheldt to the Meuse and the Rhine, the Grand Canal du Nord. When Holland was annexed by France in 1810 it was no longer needed: the work stopped and thousands of labourers lost their jobs before the canal was deep enough. Only in 1854 was the Noordervaart dug deeper, to carry the peat out of the Peel.
Langs de dijk van Meijel naar Ospel groe: Along the dyke from Meijel to Ospel a ribbon of farms grew, on land reclaimed from the Peel. In 1954 Ospeldijk became a parish village. The church of 1958 closed in 2007 and was demolished a year later; the tower was left standing. The school of 1952 closed in 2012.
Eeuwenlang staken mensen hier turf, tot: For centuries people cut peat here, until little was left of the great raised bog. What remained, with its fens, has been De Groote Peel National Park since 1993. The walks start at the De Pelen visitor centre; a steel column remembers the aircrews who died here in the war.
Kinderen uit Kreijel gingen vanaf 1829 n: From 1829 children in Kreijel went to a primitive little school; in 1861 Ospel got a public primary school, later the Heilig Hart school. In 1910 Franciscan sisters from Heythuysen came with a convent and a girls' school, the Sint-Anna school. The last sister left in 1959 and the convent became a community centre. In 1993 the two schools merged into De Schrank.
Voor zijn zilveren jubileum als pastoor: For his 25 years as Ospel's parish priest, Father Carels had a Sacred Heart statue made by Albert Verschuuren. It was placed in 1926 in a little park by the church, with a lantern at each end of the wall. The plinth reads: Come all to Me, Behold your king, I will help you.

Ospel heeft ruim vierduizend inwoners. S: Ospel has just over four thousand inhabitants. Since 1986 the first weekend of May brings the Moulin Blues festival, made by more than five hundred volunteers; B.B. King and Buddy Guy have played there. End of the tour.
